[[File:Sukunakawata-jinja, torii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
'''Sukunakawata Shrine''' (すくなかわたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kashiwara|Q873583|qid=Q873583}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. Locally it is commonly called “Shirasaka Shrine,” and maps/signs also use that name.

===Enshrined deities===
Its principal deities are {{ill|Sukunabikona|ca|Sukunabikona|fr|Sukunabikona|it|Sukuna-hikona|ja|スクナビコナ|ko|스쿠나비코나|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯕꯤꯀꯣꯅ|pl|Sukunabikona|pt|Sukunahikona|simple|Sukunabikona|sv|Suku-Na-Bikona|zh|少彥名|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikone-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takamimusubi|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|Q1073925|qid=Q1073925|lt=Shinatobe-no-Mikoto}}. ''{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}'' and ''{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}'' state “deity unknown.”

===History===
The origin of foundation is unknown. Together with nearby {{ill|Amayukawata Shrine|Q63891125|qid=Q63891125}} (Kashiwara Takaida 89), it is thought that the Tottori no Muraji, based in this area, enshrined their {{ill|Oyagami|fr|Oyagami|ja|祖神|simple|Oyagami|qid=Q85882782}}. In ''{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}'' “Tenjin Hongi,” {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sukuna-hikone-no-Mikoto}} is given as ancestral deity of Tottori no Muraji. It had been an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=official shrine}} since the time of the {{ill|Kōnin-shiki|Q17228444|qid=Q17228444}}, and in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is listed as “Sukunakawata Shrine, Ōagata District, Kawachi Province,” ranked as a small shrine.

In the medieval period it was called “Shirasaka Daimyōjin.” One theory says the place now occupied by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ninomiya Shrine}} (Andō-chō 19-9, moved to current site in Taishō after merging two shrines) was “Aza Shirasaka,” and was the original site of Sukunakawata Shrine. For that reason Ninomiya Shrine is also treated as a candidate shrine, though Ninomiya Shrine itself does not claim Shikinaisha status.

In Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked as village shrine and renamed from Shirasaka Myōjin to the current shrine name.
